sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in West New York?
sections.html:
West New York is a one-square-mile town on the Hudson Palisades where almost every sale involves a town ownership certificate, an inspection and a deed recorded in Hudson County. Only about 23 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied, so the buyer pool for a house or small building often includes landlords as well as families.

This page walks through the town's housing figures, its history and transit, the ownership certificate that gates a transfer, how the Tax Collector handles payments, and where the deed is filed.

sections.h2: How dense is West New York and what do its housing figures show?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counted 52,912 residents in 2020 and estimates 53,192 for mid-2025. They live on 0.99 square miles of land, a density of 53,231 people per square mile. The town is bordered by Guttenberg, North Bergen, Union City, Weehawken and the Hudson River.

With four out of five residents speaking another language at home, a bilingual listing and bilingual showing contact widen your audience. Rent of $1,716 against owner costs above $3,000 a month also shows why investors read a two- or three-family house by its rental income.

sections.h2: What is the history of West New York?
sections.html:
The legislature incorporated West New York as a town on July 8, 1898, replacing Union Township after a referendum held three days earlier. Early growth came from textile mills that made North Hudson the Embroidery Capital of the United States, and the population was mostly Italian and German. During the 1960s Cuban families arrived in large numbers, and the town was nicknamed Havana on the Hudson.

High-rise apartment towers rose along Boulevard East and gave the town one of the highest densities in the country. Since the 1980s the former industrial waterfront has been redeveloped into housing and the Hudson River Waterfront Walkway. The Excelsior Engine Co. No. 2 firehouse on Polk Street was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2022, a reminder that older buildings share the grid with the towers.

sections.h2: How do transit, roads and schools help a West New York listing?
sections.html:
Bergenline Avenue, with more than 300 shops and restaurants, is the commercial spine, and 60th Street is the main cross street and home of Town Hall. County Route 501 follows Kennedy Boulevard on the western edge and County Route 505 runs along Boulevard East, so the town has no state highway of its own. The Turnpike and Route 495 sit in neighboring municipalities.

  • NJ Transit buses reach the Port Authority Bus Terminal on routes 128, 154, 156, 158, 159, 165, 166 and 168, and the George Washington Bridge Bus Terminal on routes 181 and 188.
  • The Bergenline Avenue light rail station sits at the line with Union City, and the Port Imperial ferry terminal is in Weehawken.
  • Jitney buses along Bergenline Avenue run as often as one a minute.

The West New York School District serves prekindergarten through grade 12 in nine schools, ending at Memorial High School. It enrolled 8,545 students in 2019-20, and the state covers school construction costs because it is one of the former Abbott districts. The Academy of St. Joseph of the Palisades is the Catholic K-8 option. Fire protection comes from North Hudson Regional Fire and Rescue rather than a town department.

sections.h2: What does West New York require before a property can be transferred?
sections.html:
Town Code Chapter 148 makes it unlawful to sell or take title to a residential building until the town issues an ownership certificate after an inspection. It covers one-, two- and three-family homes, buildings with more than three units, commercial and mixed-use buildings, and vacant land has its own certificate. Failing to obtain a certificate carries a $1,000 fine.

  • Either the owner or the purchaser files the application, and both are liable if no certificate is obtained.
  • If the contract says the sale is as is, the signed contract goes with the application and both seller and buyer sign it.
  • The inspector checks housing, building, fire, electrical and property maintenance codes.
  • If violations will not be repaired before closing, the town may issue a temporary certificate for up to six months that cannot be renewed, and the buyer acknowledges the duty to fix them.

State fire code also requires a smoke and carbon monoxide alarm certificate before a one- or two-family home is sold. Ask the town which office issues it and schedule both inspections as soon as you have a buyer.

sections.h2: How does the West New York Tax Collector handle payments and tax sales?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector bills and collects municipal property taxes and can be reached at 201-295-5110, at 428 60th Street. The town allows a ten-day grace period, and on the eleventh day interest runs back to the legal due date. Postmarks are not accepted, so a mailed check must arrive in time.

Tax sales usually happen in December, with the date announced by the end of November. The town held an online auction for delinquent 2025 and prior-year taxes on December 17, 2025. If you are behind, ask the Tax Collector for a payoff figure before listing so the title company can clear the lien at closing.

sections.h2: Where is a West New York deed recorded and what does the seller owe the state?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded with the Hudson County Register. Hard-copy filings need a cover sheet, checks are payable to Hudson County Register, and personal or LLC checks may not exceed $200. The office phone is 201-395-4760.

The state also charges the seller a realty transfer fee. On a sale between $200,000 and $550,000, that slice is charged at $4.80 per $500, with lower and higher bands outside it, and a Graduated Percent Fee applies to consideration over $1 million. Your attorney will total it on the closing statement.

sections.h2: What are my options for selling a West New York property?
sections.html:
Most owners choose between a traditional listing, a private sale and a direct purchase by a cash buyer. The ownership certificate applies to all three.

  • A traditional listing suits a well-kept condo-style or townhouse unit that financed buyers can underwrite, but expect the inspection and lender timeline.
  • A private sale works if you already have a buyer, such as a tenant or relative, and an attorney to draft the contract.
  • A cash purchase fits a building with open violations, a tenant situation you want to avoid managing, or an estate that needs a quick close.

Ask each buyer in writing who pays for the certificate inspection and any corrections.

faqs.q: Does West New York require an inspection before a house is sold?
faqs.a: Yes. Chapter 148 of the town code requires an ownership certificate issued after an inspection before a residential building transfers. The fine for skipping it is $1,000, and both buyer and seller are responsible.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West New York building with open violations?
faqs.a: Yes, in many cases. The town may issue a temporary ownership certificate valid up to six months when violations will not be fixed before closing, and the buyer agrees to correct them. Ask the Department of Public Affairs which items qualify.

faqs.q: What is the grace period for West New York property taxes?
faqs.a: Ten days. Interest is charged from the legal due date starting on the eleventh day, and postmarks are not accepted. Call the Tax Collector at 201-295-5110 for your balance.

faqs.q: Where does a West New York deed get recorded?
faqs.a: At the Hudson County Register, not at Town Hall. Use the county's cover sheet and a check payable to Hudson County Register, and let your closing attorney or title company file it.

faqs.q: Is West New York mostly owner-occupied or rented?
faqs.a: Rented. The Census Bureau puts the owner-occupied rate at 23.0 percent for 2020-2024, with median gross rent of $1,716, so many buyers are investors who weigh rental income.
